articles.article_text: Shares of Microsoft Corp. MSFT inched 0.05% higher to $338.15 Wednesday, on what proved to be an all-around poor trading session for the stock market, with the S&P 500 Index SPX falling 0.20% to 4,446.82 and Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA falling 0.38% to 34,288.64. Microsoft Corp. closed $13.32 short of its 52-week high ($351.47), which the company achieved on June 16th. Copyright © 2026 MarketWatch, Inc. All rights reserved.

articles.title: What Going On With Microsoft Stock ? Why An EU Investigation Doesnt Bode Well - Microsoft ( NASDAQ : MSFT )
articles.title_clean: What Going On With Microsoft Stock ? Why An EU Investigation Doesnt Bode Well - Microsoft ( NASDAQ : MSFT )
articles.article_title: What's Going On With Microsoft Stock? Why An EU Investigation Doesn't Bode Well - Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) - Benzinga
articles.article_text: Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ: MSFT ) stock is trading lower Monday on the heels of a report that EU regulators are investigating the company. The Redmond, Washington-based tech giant had tried to quell antitrust scrutiny in the past , but according to Reuters, the efforts fell short. Recall Microsoft's drama with Slack , and its parent company Salesforce, Inc (NYSE: CRM ). Also Read: AI Chatbot Crackdown - Microsoft & Co. Face Regulatory Heat In Europe as ChatGPT Reignites Debate In the previous decade, Microsoft has suffered penalties worth 2.2 billion euros ($2.4 billion) for practices breaching EU competition rules, including tying or bundling two or more products. Microsoft added Teams to Office 365 in 2017 for free, with the app eventually replacing Skype for Business. Slack alleged that its rival had unfairly integrated workplace chat and video app Teams into its Office product, and asked EU officials to force Microsoft to sell Teams separately from its Office software. Microsoft started talks with the European Commission in 2022 to stave off an investigation. It recently offered to cut the price of its Office product without its Teams app. Reportedly, the European Commission sought a deeper price cut than the U.S. software giant offered. Price Action: MSFT shares traded lower by 1.11% at $336.78 on the last check Monday. Now Read: Elon Musk Gives Bill Gates An 'F' In Understanding AI © 2026 Benzinga.com. articles.title: Microsoft CEO claims Activision deal would be good for gaming industry
articles.title_clean: Microsoft CEO claims Activision deal would be good for gaming industry
articles.article_title: Microsoft CEO claims Activision deal would be good for gaming industry - MarketWatch
articles.article_text: SAN FRANCISCO — Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told a judge Wednesday that his company’s proposed $69 billion takeover of videogame-maker Activision Blizzard will be good for the gaming industry, remarks that came as he defended the deal against an attempt by federal regulators to block it. Nadella took the witness stand in a San Francisco federal court and said his goal is to get Activision ATVI games on as many platforms as possible, much as Microsoft MSFT has with its traditional software products. articles.article_text: Powered by strong returns for shares of Apple and Microsoft, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is climbing Friday morning. Shares of Apple AAPL and Microsoft MSFT have contributed to the blue-chip gauge's intraday rally, as the Dow DJIA was most recently trading 218 points (0.6%) higher. Apple's shares are up $2.90 (1.5%) while those of Microsoft have risen $4.90 (1.5%), combining for a roughly 51-point boost for the Dow. articles.article_title: U.S. reportedly plans to restrict China’s access to cloud services. That could put Amazon and Microsoft in a bind. - MarketWatch
articles.article_text: The Biden administration plans to curb China’s access to cloud computing services provided by companies such as Microsoft MSFT and Amazon.com AMZN , the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday. Citing sources characterized as familiar with the situation, the report indicated that the new rules meant U.S. companies would likely need government authorization before allowing Chinese customers access to cloud services using advanced AI chips.
